properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: hash.js@1.1.7 is a pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 implementation shipped as a transitive dependency (via elliptic) of the Hardhat/ethers toolchain. npm ci installs it; the image ships these hash algorithms whether or not the application calls them. No first-party call site found in the 5 contracts, scripts, or configs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: the secp256k1 curve/signature packages (@noble/secp256k1, secp256k1@4.x, @types/secp256k1) implement ECDSA-secp256k1 for Ethereum transaction signing. They ship as transitive deps of the Hardhat/ethers toolchain, and the first-party signing path (hardhat network accounts → ethers wallet signing) reaches them indirectly. No direct first-party import or call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the lockfile pins evp_bytestokey@^1.0.3 (OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey port — single-round MD5-based KDF) as a transitive dependency of the Hardhat/Ethers toolchain. Ships in node_modules on install; the application's own code performs no password-based key derivation, so there is no app call site. Weak KDF available in the shipped build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.3.0 provides the secp256k1 ECDSA implementation ethers v6 (via hardhat-toolbox) uses to sign this project's deployments and packet transactions. The application's signing key is configured at hardhat.config.js accounts: [process.env.PRIVATE_KEY_1] (app-level use reported as a separate finding). Distinct from scout 2's native secp256k1 package object ALG-673c8f24.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 exposed by the shipped @noble/curves@1.3.0 library; no Ed25519 call site in the application — the EVM signs with secp256k1 only. Library API surface counts as shipped algorithms; no call site is not a reason to reject.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is the classic ECDSA implementation (secp256k1/P-256, also ECDH) in the toolchain dependency tree (ethers v5 chain under hardhat-toolbox). Declared in the lockfile; no direct application call site — dependency inventory of the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: @noble/curves@1.3.0 provides secp256r1/P-256 (ECDSA/ECDH) among its curve set; it is the primary EC library of ethers v6, pulled in transitively by @nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox. Shipped with the build; no first-party P-256 call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: elliptic@6.5.4 is the classic JS elliptic-curve library (ECDH and ECDSA on secp256k1/P-256), present as a transitive dependency in the Hardhat/ethers toolchain tree. Shipped with the build; no first-party ECDH call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@1.0.3 is declared in the lockfile and exposes X25519 key agreement (plus Ed25519 and secretbox). No key-agreement call site in the application; the algorithms ship with the build regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 31 sites reviewed: lockfile entries for the PBKDF2 chain (pbkdf2@^3.0.17, @types/pbkdf2, @ethersproject/pbkdf2@5.7.0) that ethers uses for encrypted-JSON-keystore key derivation. Toolchain dependency inventory; no app-level password KDF call site, and iteration counts are chosen inside ethers' keystore code, not pinned in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 24 sites reviewed: lockfile entries for keccak@^3.0.0/3.0.2 and @ethersproject/keccak256@5.7.0 — the toolchain's Keccak-256, Ethereum's core hash. The application itself hashes with keccak256 in contracts/base/CustomChanIbcApp.sol:177/190 (reported separately) and via ethers' EIP-55 checksum. Keccak-256 is Grover-weakened only (256-bit output), not Shor-broken.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the memory-hard password KDF used by Ethereum keystore/mnemonic tooling; it ships as a transitive dependency of the Hardhat/ethers chain. No first-party scrypt call site found in application code; the shipped library remains part of the build's crypto surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: @noble/hashes@1.3.3 provides SHA-256 (plus SHA-2/3, Keccak, RIPEMD) and ships as a transitive dep of ethers v6 via hardhat-toolbox. No first-party call site found; the build still ships the implementation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 exposed by the shipped @noble/hashes@1.3.3 library; no application call site found. Library API surface counts as shipped algorithms — presence is the inventory question here; no call site is not a reason to reject. BLAKE3 is Grover-weakened only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 exposed by the shipped @noble/hashes@1.3.3 library; no application call site found (the app's hashing is Keccak-256 via the EVM opcode and ethers). Available-in-shipped-library class.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305) is exposed by the shipped tweetnacl@1.0.3 library; no application call site. The AE scheme itself is symmetric and not Shor-vulnerable; quantum relevance would come only from the key-agreement half that derives its keys, which the app never uses.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: tweetnacl@1.0.3 (verified resolving at package-lock.json:8766, with tweetnacl-util@0.15.1 at :8772) ships the NaCl primitives — XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE, Ed25519 signatures, X25519 ECDH — as a transitive dependency of the toolchain. No first-party call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider shipped with the build: @noble/hashes (SHA-2, SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE2/3, RIPEMD160, scrypt, PBKDF2, HKDF) — transitive dependency of the ethers/hardhat-toolbox chain. The build ships these algorithms whether or not the application calls them; presence is the inventory question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider shipped with the build: @noble/curves (1.2.0/1.3.0 entries at package-lock.json:259, 288, 4718) is the elliptic-curve library used by ethers v6 (via @nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox) for secp256k1 transaction signing. The first-party signing path — hardhat.config.js network accounts (env-loaded secp256k1 keys) → ethers wallet → signed transactions — reaches this library; the application itself never imports it directly.
